article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Sour Diesel × Permanent Marker
Breeder: Seed Junky Genetics
THC Content: 25%–30%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , Beta-Caryophyllene , Myrcene
Primary Flavors: Diesel fuel, chemical candy, sweet berries
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: High under favorable conditions
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Some cannabis strains whisper their aroma from the jar; Permanent Gas practically kicks the door open. Sharp diesel fumes and sour chemical notes dominate at first, yet a second layer of candy sweetness, berries, citrus peel, and creamy funk quickly appears underneath. Seed Junky Genetics created the hybrid by bringing Sour Diesel together with Permanent Marker, connecting one of marijuana’s defining fuel-heavy classics with a modern candy-gas powerhouse.

The result bridges two different eras of cannabis breeding. Its effects can be equally contrasting, beginning with an alert cerebral surge before gradually becoming heavier, warmer, and more physically relaxing. For consumers who miss unapologetically gassy weed but still enjoy the sweetness and resin production of contemporary genetics, this cultivar offers both qualities in unusually concentrated form.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct pedigree is Sour Diesel × Permanent Marker. Sour Diesel contributes the unmistakable old-school half of the equation: penetrating fuel, sour citrus, skunk, herbal earth, and an energetic cerebral character. Its loose, vigorous growth tendencies also give the hybrid some structural lift compared with many heavily Cookies-influenced plants . Although the deeper history of Sour Diesel has been debated for decades, its role here is much easier to identify through aroma and effect. The diesel side prevents the finished flower from becoming overly creamy or dessert-like.

Permanent Marker provides the modern counterweight. Seed Junky lists its genetics as ( Biscotti S1 × Sherb BX1) × Jealousy , a concentrated family of Cookies, Sherbet, Gelato, and Kush-derived traits associated with dense resin, candy sweetness, floral soap, chemical funk, and substantial potency. Rather than softening Sour Diesel, Permanent Marker adds a different type of aggression—more sweet solvent and marker ink than raw petroleum.

Putting those families together creates a cultivar whose name accurately describes its dominant direction. Sour Diesel supplies the piercing top end while Permanent Marker fills the middle with fruit, sweetness, musk, and thick chemical gas. Plants can vary, with some expressions leaning toward sour fuel and others showing more grape-candy or creamy marker funk, but the better phenotypes preserve a clear impression of both parents.
Effects and Experience

The opening portion often carries more cerebral energy than the indica-leaning classification might imply. A rapid change in mood can make conversation easier, music more absorbing, and routine surroundings feel more interesting. Thoughts may move faster for a short period, particularly in consumers accustomed to Sour Diesel’s stimulating personality. Unlike very hazy sativas, however, the mental lift usually feels more concentrated than sprawling.

Physical weight arrives behind that first wave. Shoulders loosen, the body becomes noticeably calmer, and the earlier mental momentum begins to level out. Moderate consumption can produce an unusual state in which the mind remains engaged while the body prefers to stay put. That balance makes the hybrid suitable for relaxed social evenings, movies, gaming, music, or creative activities where strict attention to detail is unnecessary.

Higher doses change the tone considerably. Strong flower can push into the upper 20% THC range or beyond, and the later stage may become heavily relaxing, sleepy, or couch-oriented. Short-term concentration can deteriorate, appetite may increase, and time can feel less structured. Consumers with limited tolerance should approach this marijuana carefully because the stimulating beginning can make the full strength easy to underestimate. Excessive THC may produce dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, mental fog, or anxiety.
Medical Benefits

Permanent Gas may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who want an effect that addresses mental tension before moving toward stronger physical relaxation. The cerebral shift can temporarily make repetitive thinking or daily stress feel less intrusive, while the later body effects may reduce awareness of muscle tightness, soreness, or generalized discomfort.

Evening use is especially logical because the experience frequently becomes heavier with time. Consumers dealing with difficulty unwinding may appreciate that gradual transition from mental stimulation into calmer physical territory. Appetite can also increase during the second half of the high, while larger servings may encourage drowsiness in people already prone to THC-related sedation.

The cultivar has not been clinically proven to treat anxiety, pain, insomnia, depression, appetite disorders, or any other medical condition. Individual response to high-THC weed depends on dose, tolerance, medications, physiology, and the chemical profile of the specific batch. Those sensitive to THC should be particularly cautious because the early cerebral stimulation can become uncomfortable when too much is consumed.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fuel is the foundation rather than a background accent. Opening a properly cured container can release an unmistakable blast of diesel, solvent, sour chemicals, and skunky earth. Permanent Marker then changes the shape of that aroma with sweeter notes reminiscent of grape candy, berries, creamy sugar, and marker ink. The contrast can resemble gasoline fumes passing through a candy store—sharp, sweet, and slightly strange in a way that experienced gas enthusiasts often seek out.

Limonene commonly contributes citrus brightness, while beta-caryophyllene reinforces pepper, spice, and the rougher fuel qualities. Myrcene can add musky earth and ripe-fruit depth, and humulene may bring a dry herbal or woody element. Exact terpene ratios differ by phenotype and grow environment, so laboratory testing of a particular harvest remains more meaningful than assuming every example will share an identical profile.

The flavor often begins cleaner than the aroma suggests. Sweet citrus, berries, and creamy candy may appear on the inhale before the smoke becomes progressively more savory. Diesel, black pepper, herbs, earth, and chemical gas expand through the exhale, leaving a persistent fuel coating across the palate. Proper drying and curing are critical because excessive heat or rapid moisture loss can flatten the sweeter volatile compounds and leave the flower tasting much more one-dimensional.
Growing Information

Permanent Gas generally flowers in roughly eight to nine weeks, with verified clone information placing the indoor window around 56–63 days. Grow reports for the Seed Junky cut describe manageable stretch of roughly one-and-a-half times its pre-flower height, along with dense, stacked flowers and substantial trichome coverage. That structure gives indoor cultivators enough vertical growth to fill space without creating the extreme height-management problems associated with some Sour Diesel expressions.

Topping and low-stress training can spread the plant across a wider canopy before the flowering stretch begins. A trellis becomes useful once the branches start carrying dense clusters, while selective removal of weak interior shoots improves light penetration. The plant’s heavy resin production also makes environmental control increasingly important late in bloom. High humidity around compact flowers can encourage mold, so dependable airflow should continue through the entire canopy.

Feeding should remain balanced rather than aggressive simply because the plant is capable of strong production. Excess nitrogen late in bloom can delay maturation and reduce final flower quality. Outdoor plants generally perform best with plenty of sunlight, good air movement, and a relatively dry early autumn, with harvest commonly arriving from late September into early October. Yield can be substantial when root space and light are abundant, but aroma intensity and resin quality are the traits most likely to justify growing this cultivar.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Permanent Gas?

Permanent Gas combines Sour Diesel with Permanent Marker. The Permanent Marker parent itself comes from (Biscotti S1 × Sherb BX1) × Jealousy, giving the finished hybrid both classic diesel genetics and a concentrated modern candy-gas background.
Who bred Permanent Gas?
Seed Junky Genetics created the widely recognized version covered here. Seed Junky currently lists Permanent Gas among its authentic seed offerings.
Is Permanent Gas indica or sativa?
It is generally treated as an indica-leaning hybrid, although the Sour Diesel parent gives the initial effects more cerebral energy than that classification might suggest.
What does Permanent Gas taste like?

Expect a strong mixture of diesel fuel, chemical funk, sweet berries, citrus, pepper, earth, and candy-like sweetness. Some examples lean heavily toward Sour Diesel, while others reveal more of Permanent Marker’s creamy fruit and solvent character.
How long does Permanent Gas take to flower?
Indoor cultivation generally requires around eight to nine weeks, with approximately 56–63 days serving as a useful range for the established cut.
Final Thoughts on Permanent Gas

Permanent Gas makes sense as a modern strain precisely because it refuses to abandon the flavors that helped define an earlier generation of cannabis. Sour Diesel brings raw petroleum, sour citrus, skunk, and cerebral energy, while Permanent Marker contributes dense resin, candy sweetness, creamy funk, and a peculiar chemical quality of its own. Instead of polishing the gas away, the cross layers one form of pungency on top of another.

That combination creates more than a loud aroma. Consumers receive a high that can begin alert and euphoric before settling into substantial body relaxation, while cultivators get a manageable flowering period, dense trichome-heavy buds, and enough production potential for serious indoor or outdoor work. In a market filled with fruit, candy, and dessert weed, Permanent Gas stands apart by using those modern flavors to reinforce rather than replace diesel. The result is a cultivar built for people who want their cannabis sweet, potent, and unmistakably fuel-driven.
